findings.kind: previous historical finding reconnected by independent current source
findings.condition: A public positions, previous, or velocities Buffer or its mutable logical fields is replaced or modified independently of the private particle count, capacity or cached masses; native acceptance and actual callers are not established.
findings.trace: Particles exposes all three buffers while retaining private count, capacity and inverse_masses. Buffer exposes native handle, size and usage; Buffer::write takes &self, so a separately constructed upload may mutate public positions without updating the host mass cache. Solver binds those buffers with the retained count. On successful device write and readback, cached inverse_masses() and read_inverse_masses() may disagree; write_positions reuploads the cached mass words. If a shorter replacement produces successful readback, read_positions takes at most count rather than checking exact length, and the solver still dispatches that count. No native acceptance, real call path, data race, runtime result or panic is asserted.
findings.direction: Resolve aggregate ownership and checked whole-buffer/count/mass correspondence, including explicit native views and checked replacement/readback; preserve intentional raw words, zero-particle state and pinned inverse mass.
findings.dedup: This conditional current source observation and cached-mass consequence belong to the prior F082 relationship; no new accepted count is proposed.

findings.kind: previous historical finding reconnected by independent current source
findings.condition: On a host permitting a position slice length at least 2^32 and sufficient resources to reach the operation, positions.len() as u32 wraps before the capacity comparison and before count assignment; earlier allocation or native failure may stop the path.
findings.trace: For hypothetical length 2^32, the narrowing becomes 0; from_positions asks new for 0 capacity, which is raised to 1; write sees equal slice lengths and the narrowed capacity check does not reject 0 > 1, before attempting huge packing and native upload. No huge allocation, upload or fixture was attempted; native behavior and real production reachability are unknown. write_positions also narrows for its equality check but then calls write, whose full host-length mass comparison is a separate gate.
findings.direction: Check host-to-native executable count and bytes before narrowing and before native allocations; preserve legitimate zero, exact host diagnostics and normal supported layouts.
findings.dedup: Same particle length-admission boundary as F073-SUPPLEMENT-001; do not count anew.

findings.kind: 059 historical open connected contract; independently traced 95e
findings.condition: Caller-facing error taxonomy is undecided; producer and native consumers outside selected windows remain open.
findings.trace: write first checks full position/mass lengths, then narrowed capacity; write_positions first checks narrowed count and then delegates to write. Public ParticlePositions::new separately checks equal lengths, but when nested under write its equal-length gate follows an equivalent outer check. Identical diagnostic text does not establish common owner or identical first failure. Shell::new invokes mesh and material validation, rejects empty mesh, derives inverse masses and invokes from_positions; selected source does not establish other callers or full native error classification.
findings.direction: Keep separate first-gate predicates and trace real API/error consumers before deciding a shared or separate typed reason owner; do not preserve current literal prose as a compatibility constraint.
findings.dedup: Historical open contract; neither closure nor new unique count proposed.

nonfindings.text: write_positions takes the cache temporarily and restores it after write returns, including normal Result::Err. It does not by itself establish loss of the host masses on an ordinary Err; panic/unwinding behavior has not been assessed.

The wrapper Buffer::write immediately calls BufferUpload::write_to and then returns Ok(()); this body supplies no ordinary Err branch. Thus earlier concern that its ? alone proves a later returned Err after an earlier upload is not established. Native queue validation, panics, device errors, and loss of transactional consistency are unproved, not ruled out.

Position/mass and velocity records are intentionally distinct nominal types, even though the native records have similar-sized word layouts. Position construction enforces equal lengths before zip; at_rest derives the velocity count from positions; packed source does not promise valid finite state and is not proof the compile-fail doctest passes.

ParticleInverseMass explicitly preserves arbitrary native float words; validity is a separate classification and +/- zero is intentionally prescribed. Rejecting NaNs or zeros at every native readback would impose an unproven policy.
On successful write the previous position buffer is reset and velocities are uploaded at rest; this supports the prior bounded pose-reset rejection, without establishing device execution.

open_questions: What concrete consumer or supported extension replaces buffers or uploads particle mass words directly, and does that producer require host/device coherence?
What exact policy should govern externally constructed particle positions and inverse masses, including numerical validity and native readback?
Can valid supported host populations exceed native u32 count or native byte/dispatch limits after real allocation boundaries, and where should each limit be admitted?

What native queue validation, failure, panic and publication semantics apply for sequential writes; may any successfully submitted first write coexist with later failure? This remains outside source-only proof.
What is the appropriate error taxonomy for each distinct first predicate, and which actual callers consume it?
Do all alternate consumers, previous buffer mutability and retained capacity changes share the same aggregate authority? No full call graph was attempted.
